clue.text: Hawk biting head of raw fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the next word is kept
something biting closes its jaws around what it bites, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to hawk goods is to tout them, pushing them on passers-by
the opening letter of raw

explanation.surface: A bird of prey sinks its beak into an uncooked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawk looks like the bird, but here it is a verb meaning to sell aggressively, as a ticket tout does.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a common freshwater game species related to salmon.

clue.text: Pragmatic type on a register

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
taken as written
a register is a list of names

explanation.surface: A practical person is entered on an official roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they actually are, being practical rather than idealistic.

clue.text: A thingy: utensil used at once

indicators.note: something used has been handled and knocked about, so these letters end up in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Some gadget or kitchen tool gets put to work straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unhesitatingly means acting immediately without pause, with no delay or doubt.

clue.text: Go south with pack

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
to pack a bag tight is to cram it

explanation.surface: Someone heads south taking a rucksack along.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a curt command meaning leave at once, the same as an impatient instruction to go away.

clue.text: Empty garage it seems for spice

blocks.note: a garage looks empty when its car is away

explanation.surface: An empty garage seems to call for a spice.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a playful description of the scene rather than a synonym: CAR + AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is an aromatic seed used to flavour rye bread and seed cake.

clue.text: Off carrying metal on the wagon

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it within, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: someone off work is absent
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: Metal goods being carried off on a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: On the wagon is an idiom for giving up alcohol; wagon misleadingly matches carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the wagon refrains from drinking alcohol, which is exactly what abstinent means.

clue.text: Highly valued fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: a prize job or role is described with this adjective
second meaning: a stone fruit, purple or yellow

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a prized fruit; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is an especially desirable one, and the plum is a common orchard stone fruit.

clue.text: Propose this to queen surprisingly succeeding father

indicators.note: something turning out surprisingly is not as expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: pop is an informal word for dad
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man proposes this to the queen after his father has had a go.
explanation.walkthrough: Succeeding means following, so the rearranged letters come after the father.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop the question is the idiom for asking someone to marry you.

clue.text: Each dish fills one

indicators.note: something that fills a space sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
a pie is a baked dish

explanation.surface: Every serving dish is filled with one portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for every one individually, as in costing a pound per item.

clue.text: Single chap, bishop with cholera, unfortunately

indicators.note: something going unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are knocked out of their proper order

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman catches a nasty disease, which is bad luck for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, someone not yet wed.

clue.text: Mushy prune eaten by operative

indicators.note: food that is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a secret operative or agent is a spy
to prune a branch is to lop it off

explanation.surface: A soft dried plum is swallowed by a working man.
explanation.walkthrough: Prune looks like the dried fruit, which suits mushy, but it is the gardening verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy food is wet, soft and runny, with no firm texture to it.

clue.text: Stupid problem, fare from China

blocks.note: a dim person is slow-witted
a sum is an arithmetic problem set in class

explanation.surface: A foolish difficulty arises over Chinese cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Cantonese dumplings and snacks, a well-known style of Chinese food.

clue.text: Ski resort ref?

blocks.note: first meaning: a well-known Canadian winter-sports town in British Columbia
second meaning: a referee is someone who blows a whistle

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a query about an official at a ski resort; the question mark flags that the referee meaning is a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler hosted the 2010 Winter Olympic skiing, and a match official signals with blasts on a whistle.

clue.text: Associate backing infant to the greatest degree

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A partner supports a baby as much as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing means the associate comes behind the infant, supporting it from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely or utterly, entirely and without any reservation.

clue.text: Criminal in scarlet pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are treated as a mess to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook is spotted wearing red trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like the noun for trousers (or, in Britain, underwear), but it is slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, so a larcenist is a thief, a kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Cricket team left uniform on back of vehicle

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of vehicle
L is the standard abbreviation for left
something uniform is even, with no variation

explanation.surface: A cricket side leaves its kit on the back of the team bus.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-style reading, on means placed after, so the vehicle's last letter comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side has eleven players, so the number is a standard name for the team.

clue.text: Sommelier, for example, one inspired by drink

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so one piece is drawn inside the other

blocks.note: water is the plainest drink
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wine expert finds inspiration in what he drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a wine steward who serves diners at table, so is one kind of restaurant server.

clue.text: Article spotted reportedly, native American

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or told, so the word is judged by speech

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
something spotted is patchy, marked in places

explanation.surface: A news story says someone was seen, describing a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted suggests seen, but it means marked with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Indigenous peoples of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Possible declaration in seat after significant figure returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: a ton is a hundred, a notable figure in cricket or speed
your seat is your backside, the rump

explanation.surface: A statement made in Parliament after an important person has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the seat behind the returned figure. In bridge, the bidding declarations name a trump suit or none.
explanation.definitionFit: No-trump is a bid in bridge proposing the hand be played without any trump suit.

clue.text: Personality lacking in expertise?

blocks.note: first meaning: a well-known person, a celebrity
second meaning, read playfully as two words: unskilled, without competence

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense needs the answer split into two words, NOT ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is an important or famous figure, and someone not able lacks the skill to do something.

clue.text: Two girls — is one capped?

blocks.note: Pat and Ella are two girls' names

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether one of a pair of girls has won an international cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Capped hints at sport, but the answer is the bone covered by the kneecap.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a bone that caps the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Stance in reforms, most prudent

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters are given a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The wisest position to take on reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd and careful, so the superlative describes whoever is most careful and wise.

clue.text: Old coin placed inside seed

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other's letters

blocks.note: a pea is the seed of a pod plant
to place something is to set it down

explanation.surface: An antique coin has been planted inside a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain until the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Italian city where a drink served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A town in Italy where a drink is brought to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is a Tuscan city famous for its leaning bell tower.

clue.text: Hot food I found beside cold

blocks.note: a chill is a cold feeling, or a cold you catch
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds spicy food next to something cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot and cold set up a contrast in the surface, but hot here means spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli is a fiery pepper, and also the spicy stew named after it.

clue.text: Old prison cell: it’s abysmal, some recalled

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters
to recall is to call back, so the letters are taken from the end towards the start

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A former inmate remembers a dreadful jail cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts after the C of cell and ends at the AB of abysmal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress-jail stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Alloy, bargain by the sound of it?

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is judged on how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a real bargain is called a steal

explanation.surface: A cheap metal deal seems almost too good to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon, the commonest mixed metal.

clue.text: Convenient rewriting of panto

indicators.note: rewriting a script reworks it, so the letters of the word are set down in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A handy new version of a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto, short for pantomime, is a British family Christmas stage comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is readily available whenever needed, like beer from a barrel.
